note: Salzburg AG Sohlstufe Lehen on the Salzach in Salzburg city, 13.7 MW, 81 GWh/a, 2013 (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wasserkraftwerk_Sohlstufe_Lehen); absent from powerplantmatching

Name: Opponitz
note: Wien Energie Kraftwerk Opponitz on the Ybbs, 12.5 MW after the 2018 revitalisation, 66.8 GWh/a (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kraftwerk_Opponitz; Anlagenregister 12.4 MW at 3342 Opponitz); absent from powerplantmatching

Name: Untere Sill
note: IKB Kraftwerk Untere Sill in Innsbruck, 28 MW bottleneck capacity (https://www.ikb.at/unternehmen/kraftwerke/kraftwerk-untere-sill; Anlagenregister 28 MW at 6020 Innsbruck); absent from powerplantmatching; approximate coordinates

Name: Spullersee
note: OeBB Bahnstromkraftwerk Spullersee, powerhouse at Danoefen/Wald am Arlberg (Dalaas) on the Alfenz, 36 MW, 1925, modernised 2021, 16.7 Hz railway grid (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spullersee; powerhouse coordinates OSM way 266746972); absent from powerplantmatching; the lake itself lies in the Lech basin, the water is turbined into the Alfenz

Name: Goessnitz
note: KELAG Laufkraftwerk Goessnitz of the Fragant group, 2x4 MW, 1962, at Flattach next to Ausserfragant (https://openinframap.org/stats/area/Austria/plants/89027365; https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kraftwerksgruppe_Fragant); absent from powerplantmatching; coordinates from OpenInfraMap (an earlier approximate location fell outside the Moell catchment)

Name: Kolbnitz Reisseck Kreuzeck
note: Verbund Krafthaus Kolbnitz of the Reisseck-Kreuzeck group: Jahresspeicher Reisseck 68 MW, Tagesspeicher Gondelwiese 23.2 MW, Tagesspeicher Kreuzeck 45 MW, no pumps (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kraftwerksgruppe_Rei%C3%9Feck-Kreuzeck); ppm only holds Reisseck II; KLIEN section 80603 C_current 138 MW equals these plants

Name: Marchtrenk
note: Energie AG Laufkraftwerk Marchtrenk on the Traun, 42.8 MW, 173 GWh/a, 1980 (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_von_Wasserkraftwerken_in_Ober%C3%B6sterreich); absent from powerplantmatching; approximate coordinates; KLIEN section 60205 C_current 117 MW = Traun-Pucking 46 + Marchtrenk 43 + Lambach 14 + small plants

Name: Lambach
note: Energie AG Laufkraftwerk Lambach on the Traun, 13.9 MW, 73 GWh/a, 1999 (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_von_Wasserkraftwerken_in_Ober%C3%B6sterreich); absent from powerplantmatching; approximate coordinates

Name: Gmunden
note: Energie AG Laufkraftwerk Gmunden at the Traunsee outflow, 12.2 MW, 48 GWh/a, 1968 (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_von_Wasserkraftwerken_in_Ober%C3%B6sterreich); absent from powerplantmatching; approximate coordinates; KLIEN section 60203 C_current 13.9 MW

Name: Traunleiten
note: Wels Strom GmbH (eww) Laufkraftwerk Traunleiten at Steinhaus bei Wels on the Traun, new plant 'ueber 18 MW' and 91 GWh/a commissioned 2020 replacing the 1899 plant of just under 10 MW (https://www.eww.at/ueber-uns/wels-strom-gmbh/erzeugung/kraftwerktraunleiten; https://www.land-oberoesterreich.gv.at/222622.htm); absent from powerplantmatching and above the Kleinwasserkraft class; closes most of the KLIEN catchment 60205 gap (117 MW = Traun-Pucking 46 + Marchtrenk 43 + Traunleiten 18 + small plants)

Name: Partenstein
note: Energie AG Speicherkraftwerk Partenstein on the Grosse Muehl (weekly storage Langhalsen, 2x19.6 MW Francis + tail stage), 33.8 MW bottleneck capacity, 102 GWh/a, 1924 (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speicherkraftwerk_Partenstein); absent from powerplantmatching; KLIEN catchment 60105 C_current 36 MW = Partenstein + small plants

Name: Braz
note: OeBB Bahnstromkraftwerk Braz at Innerbraz, lower stage below Spullersee on the Alfenz, 2x15 MW, built 1947-54, 16.7 Hz railway grid (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_von_Bahnstromanlagen_in_%C3%96sterreich; https://www.vol.at/naturgefahrenschutzdamm-fuer-kraftwerk-braz/6014089; coordinates OSM way 119877457); absent from powerplantmatching and from the Anlagenregister; KLIEN catchment 10102 C_current 83 MW = Spullersee 36 + Braz 30 + Kloesterle 16 + small plants

Name: Kloesterle
note: illwerke vkw Kraftwerk Kloesterle on the Alfenz, diversion plant with 2x8 MW Francis, 324 m head, 48 GWh/a, 1997 (https://www.illwerkevkw.at/kw-kloesterle; coordinates OSM way 126215500); absent from powerplantmatching; run-of-river (no reservoir; confirmed by AGGM 2026-09-08)

Name: Obervermuntwerk I
note: illwerke vkw Obervermuntwerk I (Silvretta reservoir to Vermunt reservoir), still operating next to Obervermuntwerk II, 36 MW per operator (29 MW per Wikipedia/OSM), 1943 (https://www.illwerkevkw.at/geschaeftsfelder/wasserkraft/speicherkraftwerke/obervermuntwerk-I); absent from powerplantmatching; KLIEN catchment 10101 non-pumped capacity 715 MW = Kops I 288 + Rodund I 198 + Vermunt 170 + Obervermunt I 36 + Latschau 9 + small plants

Name: Schneiderau
note: OeBB Bahnstromkraftwerk Schneiderau, middle stage of the Stubachtal group, 2x17.5 MW, 1937-41, 16.7 Hz railway grid (https://openinframap.org/stats/area/Austria/plants/94149217; https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kraftwerksgruppe_Stubachtal); absent from powerplantmatching and from the Anlagenregister

Name: Uttendorf I
note: OeBB Bahnstromkraftwerk Uttendorf I, lower stage of the Stubachtal group sharing the building with Uttendorf II (66 MW, 1991, present in powerplantmatching as 'Uttendorf'). Source of the 27 MW: AGGM derivation - OpenStreetMap gives 93 MW for both Uttendorf stages together (https://openinframap.org/stats/area/Austria/plants/28620626) and Uttendorf II is 66 MW (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kraftwerksgruppe_Stubachtal), hence 93 - 66 = 27 MW for stage I; no source states the figure directly. Cross-check: Enzingerboden 81 + Schneiderau 35 + Uttendorf 93 + Gruensee 0.5 = 209.5 MW against the KLIEN catchment 40302 non-pumped capacity of 212 MW

Name: Plankenau
note: Energie AG Oberoesterreich Flusskraftwerk Plankenau (Grossarl II) at St. Veit im Pongau on the Grossarler Ache, diversion plant 5.2 + 7.2 MW, 56.7 GWh/a, 1922 (https://wiki.sn.at/wiki/Flusskraftwerk_Plankenau); absent from powerplantmatching and above the Kleinwasserkraft class; KLIEN catchment 40409 C_current 31 MW = Plankenau 11.2 + Grossarl 6.4 + Oflek 2.3 + small plants

Name: Kitzloch
note: Achen Kraftwerke AG (Salzburger Aluminium group, industrial self-supply, therefore in neither powerplantmatching nor the Anlagenregister): Kraftwerk Rauris-Kitzloch (1952/53, 3.3 km tunnel, 221.5 m head, 8 m3/s, 90 GWh/a) plus the old Flusskraftwerk Kitzloch (1903, about 5.9 MW, 15 GWh/a) at the same site on the Rauriser Ache (https://wiki.sn.at/wiki/Flusskraftwerk_Kitzloch; https://wiki.sn.at/wiki/Achen_Kraftwerke_AG). Source of the 21.9 MW: AGGM derivation - no source publishes the installed capacity; 8 m3/s x 221.5 m x 9.81 x 0.85 gives about 16 MW for the new plant, plus 5.9 MW for the old one, which matches the KLIEN catchment 40404 capacity of 21.9 MW; 105 GWh/a over 21.9 MW are 4,800 full-load hours

Name: Wagrain St Johann
note: Energie AG Oberoesterreich Kraftwerk Wagrain-St. Johann on the Wagrainer (lower Kleinarler) Ache, diversion plant with daily storage Ginau, 241 m head, 16.4 MW, 63.1 GWh/a, 1988 (https://wiki.sn.at/wiki/Flusskraftwerk_Wagrain_-_St._Johann; https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_von_Wasserkraftwerken_im_Bundesland_Salzburg); absent from powerplantmatching; the powerhouse coordinates fall into the KLIEN catchment 40501 Kleinarler Ache (C_current 21.3 MW = Wagrain 16.4 + Kleinarl 1.8 + Spannberg 1.7 + Grafenberg 1.0)

Name: Wiesberg
note: Donau Chemie AG Kraftwerk Wiesberg (industrial self-supply for the Landeck carbide works, in neither powerplantmatching nor the Anlagenregister), diversion plant with intakes on the Trisanna and Rosanna, 17 MW, 77 GWh/a, 1901/02, rebuilt after the 2005 flood and extended 2019/20 (https://www.bernard-gruppe.com/de/2020/09/25/wasserkraftwerk-wiesberg-wiederaufbau-und-modernisierung/; https://austria-forum.org/af/AustriaWiki/Landeck_(Tirol)); KLIEN catchment 30402 Trisanna counts 26.1 MW = Wiesberg 17 + the Gemeinschaftskraftwerk Paznaun (8.9 MW, under construction, commissioning 2027) which is not part of the 2025 fleet

Name: Schwarzach Osttirol
note: TIWAG Kraftwerk Schwarzach in the Defereggental, diversion plant with intake at Hopfgarten and powerhouse at Huben, 263.8 m head, 9.9 MW in 2007 and 16.9 MW / 83 GWh/a after the second unit of 2021-2023 (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schwarzach_(Isel); https://www.dolomitenstadt.at/2021/01/15/tiwag-erweitert-kraftwerk-an-der-schwarzach/); absent from powerplantmatching; the cooperative plants of the valley (Trojeralmbach, Zwenewaldbach, Gruenalmbach) are in the Anlagenregister small-hydro class

Name: Fulpmes
note: OeBB-Infrastruktur Schachtkraftwerk Fulpmes on the Ruetz (Stubaital), 182 m head, 2 Francis, 15.4 MW, 74 GWh/a, 1983, 16.7 Hz railway grid (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruetzkraftwerk; https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_von_Wasserkraftwerken_in_%C3%96sterreich); absent from powerplantmatching and from the Anlagenregister like all OeBB plants; KLIEN catchment 30503 Ruetz counts 20.8 MW = Fulpmes 15.4 + IKB Ruetzkraftwerk Schoenberg 6 (small-hydro class)

Name: Lutz Oberstufe
note: illwerke vkw Kraftwerk Lutz Oberstufe, storage plant fed from the Raggal reservoir on the Lutz (Grosses Walsertal), 130 m head, 19.3 MW, 73-79 GWh/a, 1967 (https://www.illwerkevkw.at/geschaeftsfelder/wasserkraft/speicherkraftwerke/lutz-oberstufe; https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kraftwerk_Oberstufe_Lutz); absent from powerplantmatching; the powerhouse coordinates at Ludesch fall into the KLIEN catchment 10103 Lutz (C_current 23.5 MW = Lutz Oberstufe 19.3 + small plants); the Unterstufe (8.6 MW, Bludesch) belongs to the small-hydro class and the Ill catchment
